This seems weird, though it may not be related to the crash. Do you have this in the logs also with 4.3.stable and previous 4.4.dev snapshots?

```
: CommandLine Error: Option 'help-list' registered more than once!
LLVM ERROR: inconsistency in registered CommandLine options
Aborted (core dumped)
```

So this is the main error. An internal LLVM error like this typically means a driver bug, in your case a Mesa issue.

I see you have Mesa 22.3.0-devel:
```
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 22.3.0-devel - Compatibility - Using Device: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (navi22, LLVM 15.0.3, DRM 3.49, 5.15.0-126-generic)
```

Did you install this manually from a PPA or compile from source? A devel version of Mesa would likely not be shipped by Ubuntu in its LTS version.

In fact, Ubuntu 22.04 seems to have a much newer Mesa version, you might just need to update?

I would suggest to try Godot 4.4-dev5 on the latest Ubuntu LTS 22.04 LiveCD, if possible. If it crashes, it would underline something with your machine. If it doesn't crash, it would point towards a driver issue.

Don't hesitate to share your findings here.

@knucklesncs These packages with `amdgpu` in the name and version `1:22.3.0.50401` don't seem to be provided by Ubuntu. I suspect they're an old installation of the confusingly named AMDGPU (PRO) proprietary driver from AMD (presumably from https://www.amd.com/en/support/download/linux-drivers.html), which is now quite old and out of date compared to the rest of your Mesa (open source drivers) setup.

On Linux, there's not much reason to use the proprietary AMDGPU PRO driver as the open source driver which is part of the kernel + mesa (also named AMDGPU) is full-featured and maintained by AMD engineers. So I would suggest removing the packages with version `1:22.3.0.50401`, doing a round of normal `apt-get update`, and you might end up with a much better driver situation.
I just tested `Godot_v4.4-dev6_linux.x86_64` and I got the `libX11.so.6: undefined symbol: XFreeThreads`, however the editor is starting up.

> I just tested `Godot_v4.4-dev6_linux.x86_64` and I got the `libX11.so.6: undefined symbol: XFreeThreads`, however the editor is starting up.

Thanks for testing. Yeah the "undefined symbol: XFreeThreads" error is not what's causing the crash here for @knucklesncs - it's very likely caused by their mismatch between recent-ish Mesa and outdated AMDGPU PRO drivers.

The XFreeThreads warning is probably harmless and was likely caused by #98976 in 4.4-dev5 and later.
I'll close this as debugging so far points at a user system configuration issue, not a Godot bug.

Thanks for the explanations and help, everyone!
I upgraded my system to the next LTS and removed the mismatching driver versions, and the 4.4-dev5 is working for me now.
